**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean stems (mid-plant level, held by hand) showing reddish-brown to brown elongated discoloration along internodes
- Damage concentrated at and around nodes
- Upper stem portions appear dead/dried
- No visible black fruiting bodies, no white mycelium, no linear pycnidia rows
- No leaf symptoms visible — image focused on stem

**Reference comparison:**
- **Phytophthora**: Reference shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward, with nodal brown discoloration (bottom-right panel) closely matching the reddish-brown elongated stem lesions in the test image
- **Anthracnose**: Late-season dry golden stems/pods — doesn't match the reddish-brown active stem lesion pattern
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown lesions typically at/near soil line only — test image shows damage higher on plant
- **Diaporthe**: Requires visible black pycnidia in linear rows — none clearly visible
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Characterized by internal pith browning — external stem lesions here don't match
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Gray-streaked stems with microsclerotia — not the reddish-brown pattern shown
- **Fusarium**: Dark black roots, pale stem interior — not matching

**Conclusion:** The reddish-brown to chocolate-brown elongated stem discoloration extending along multiple internodes and nodes, with upper plant dieback, best matches **Phytophthora**. This is the canonical diagnostic feature — brown stem discoloration moving upward from the soil line.
